key_insight: A recursive hybrid simulator combines Feynman path-summing across qubit partitions with stabilizer-frame simulation on each half to exactly simulate near-Clifford circuits more efficiently than prior cut-count-based methods.
engineering_relevance: The paper provides a practical backend-selection and partitioning strategy that can materially speed up exact quantum circuit simulation while handling memory limits via automatic dense-state fallback.
method: Binary-tree recursive bipartitioning of the circuit
Stabilizer-frame simulation on each leaf with dense fallback when memory is exceeded
Cost-model-driven partition selection using stabilizer-frame and readout costs
evidence_signal: On a structured n=16 benchmark, the method outperformed monolithic stabilizer-frame simulation by 92x–17,645x and beat a production state-vector simulator by up to 47.9x, while dense state vectors won for adversarial circuits beyond a crossover near n/2 cross-cut gates.
watch_item: Performance depends strongly on the circuit structure and partition quality, so the hybrid method may lose to dense state-vector simulation on adversarial instances with many cross-cut gates.
paper_title: Adaptive Multi-Backend Simulation of Near-Clifford Quantum Circuits via Spatial Stabilizer-Frame Partitioning
